type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.

When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. content.text:
The suite fails this job's bar. The main reason is copy-pasted helpers across the test files. The second is one real gap: no test catches the browser script treating any 2xx reply as success.

**What I checked:** all 12 files listed, read in full against `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md`. I also ran `npm test`: 474 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, about 6 s. I tried to look for the `res.ok` gap in `.team/near-miss/` with a shell command, which was denied. A file search confirmed no test covers it.

**What is good**
- Spec messages are compared exactly as `{ error: message }`, with the exact Content-Type.
- Edge cases sit right at the limits: 10000 vs 10001 bytes (plain, multi-byte and chunked), titles of 80 vs 81 characters (including emoji), leap years, 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, and touching bookings.
- The order of the booking rules is tested as a ladder (each case breaks every later rule too).
- Some tests target specific wrong implementations: the earliest-starting overlap is named rather than the first created, `trim` is used rather than `trimEnd`, and ids are not used up by failed POSTs.
- The fake browser records any API the spec does not allow.
- Temp folders and server processes are always cleaned up in `finally`/`after`, and every startup and exit has a time limit.

**What needs fixing**

1. **Duplication (the main failure).**
   - The same error-check function is written five times:
     - `api-routing.test.mjs:10`
     - `api-bookings-list.test.mjs:9`
     - `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:57`
     - `api-booking-fields.test.mjs:45`
     - `server-persistence.test.mjs:39` (as `assertError`)
   - About 50 lines are copied between `api-booking-rules.test.mjs:8-71` and `api-booking-fields.test.mjs:8-59`: `SIX_KEYS`, `MSG`, `dayCounter`/`freshDate`, `booking`, `label`, `useServer`, `assertCreated`.
   - Other repeats: `listBookings`, the temp-folder-plus-server wrappers, the server setup/teardown in `api-routing` and `api-bookings-list`, and `assertOnlyAllowedApis`.
   - `postWith` (`api-booking-rules.test.mjs:33`) repeats what `postBooking`'s `contentType` option already does.

2. **Missing test: "error status" means "not the exact success status".** Every error case uses 4xx or 5xx. A script using `res.ok` or `status >= 400` would pass the whole suite.

3. **Smaller gaps.**
   - The Cancel 404/500 test never checks that the button is enabled again.
   - Label, h1 and button text is compared after `.trim()`, which is looser than the "exactly this text" the spec gives.

4. **Possible flakiness.** `freePort()` frees a port and reuses it later, which can race with other processes. The port-3000 test checks the port, then binds it, and skips itself if it is busy.

5. **Readability.** The title cases contain invisible Unicode characters (NBSP, U+3000, BOM, U+2028/2029, zero-width space). `JSON.stringify` keeps most of them invisible, so several tests end up with identical names such as `accepts " x "`.

## GRADE
Overall: 8.1/10
Verdict: fail
structure: 8 — helpers are well split, but each file sets up its own server and has its own module-level `dayCounter` state
naming: 7 — `api-booking-rules` and `api-booking-fields` both cover booking rules (1-5 vs 6-10), short names (`r`, `s`, `ls`, `fd`, `lis`), several tests share the same name
duplication: 5 — the error check is copied 5 times; about 50 lines of helpers are copied between the two booking-rule files; `postWith` repeats `postBooking`
size: 9 — every file is under 300 lines and every function is well under 50
errors: 8 — time limits and kill/cleanup in `finally`, but `exists()` swallows every error and an empty error handler has no comment
tests: 8 — exact spec values and strong limit cases, but no 2xx-but-wrong-status case, the Cancel error test does not check the button is enabled again, `.trim()` loosens exact text checks, port races
security: 10 — no secrets; child process gets a cleaned environment; temp folders only
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs
Fixes:
- test/api-routing.test.mjs:10, test/api-bookings-list.test.mjs:9, test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:57, test/api-booking-fields.test.mjs:45, test/server-persistence.test.mjs:39 move the error check into test/helpers/server-harness.mjs as `assertJsonError` and import it
- test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:8-71 and test/api-booking-fields.test.mjs:8-59 move SIX_KEYS, MSG, freshDate, booking, label, useServer and assertCreated into a shared helper (e.g. test/helpers/booking-api.mjs); keep one date counter per process
- test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:33 delete `postWith`; use `postBooking(port, value, { contentType, raw })`, which already sends no header for `contentType: undefined`
- test/api-routing.test.mjs:26, test/server-persistence.test.mjs:33 share one `listBookings`; share the temp-folder-plus-server wrappers (server-startup.test.mjs:16-33, server-persistence.test.mjs:13-27) and the server setup/teardown (api-routing.test.mjs:37-46, api-bookings-list.test.mjs:53-62) through the harness
- test/app-startup-list.test.mjs:7, test/app-actions.test.mjs:5 export `assertOnlyAllowedApis` from test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs
- test/app-actions.test.mjs:117 add cases where a POST gets 200 and a DELETE gets 200 with `{error:'x'}`, and test/app-startup-list.test.mjs:60 add a rooms/list fetch that gets 201 or 204; each must show the error, so that `res.ok` / `status >= 400` fail
- test/app-actions.test.mjs:191-199 assert `button.disabled === false` after a Cancel 404/500
- test/page-html.test.mjs:41,44,77,85,97 compare text without `.trim()`, or only remove the whitespace the page's own markup adds, so `Room ` or ` Book` text would fail
- test/server-startup.test.mjs:132-138 drop the free-then-reuse `freePort()` race (e.g. retry on EADDRINUSE, or test the leading zero with `PORT=00` plus the existing `00000` case)
- test/server-startup.test.mjs:115-116 the check-then-bind of port 3000 races, and the test silently skips; note this or make the skip reason visible in CI
- test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs:244,256-260 write the invisible characters as `\u00a0`, `\u3000\ufeff`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`, `\u200b` and give each case a unique test name
- test/server-persistence.test.mjs:30 only return false on `err.code === 'ENOENT'` and rethrow anything else
- test/server-persistence.test.mjs:229 comment that the empty error handler is there on purpose (the abort is what the test does)
- test/app-startup-list.test.mjs:96 use `instanceof TextNode` (exported from fake-dom) instead of `constructor.name`
